name: CCA Lagos (Centre for Contemporary Art)
funding: Founded 2007 by Bisi Silva with her own money. A March 2022 Sotheby's benefit auction raised US$1M toward a permanent home in Yaba. It publishes no funder list.
watch: Founded in 2007 by curator Bisi Silva to focus on visual art research, experimental installation and photography in Nigeria. Runs the Asiko International Art School and one of West Africa's largest visual art libraries.
records_note: Its site names its trustees and staff, but posts no annual report, accounts or funder list.

name: CEAAC
funding: DRAC Grand Est, Région Grand Est, Collectivité européenne d'Alsace and the City of Strasbourg. One listed patron, SAS Neunreiter. Residency partners are foreign art centres.
watch: European centre for contemporary artistic action, in the former Neunreiter store. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; the about page names the elected board, four public funders, five networks and one patron (SAS Neunreiter), all undated.

name: Cemeti - Institute for Art and Society
funding: Artist-founded 1988; residency partners named on Res Artis are Mondriaan Fund, Goethe-Institut, NAC Singapore and Australia Council (undated).
records_note: Its site names the Mondriaan Fund as a 2024 residency partner and shows five founders and staff; no reports or accounts are posted.

name: Center of Contemporary Art Tbilisi (Tbilisi Triennial)
funding: A small independent non-profit and organiser of the Tbilisi Triennial, funded by foreign governments and foundations (Swiss SDC, German Foreign Office, Danish funds) and individual donors.
watch: Founded by Wato Tsereteli in 2010. Nearly all its funding is foreign, so Georgia's 2025 foreign-agents law exposes it.
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; the supporters page names nine key benefactors and individual donors with no date; no board is listed.

name: Centraal Museum
watch: The page gives no amounts or dates for the three. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: It posts annual reports and accounts for 2018 to 2025 and a named supervisory board; the 2025 report lists funders and corporate partners by name.

name: Centrale Fies
funding: Autonomous Province of Trento (Provincia Autonoma di Trento), Italian Ministry of Culture, Creative Europe; non-profit foundation.
watch: A 1911 hydroelectric plant in the alpine Sarca Valley, now an independent research center for contemporary performance.

name: Centre d'Art la Panera
funding: City Council of Lleida (Ajuntament de Lleida), Generalitat de Catalunya; public contemporary art centre.
watch: Public contemporary art and artist publishing center in a 12th-century grain exchange.

name: Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito
funding: Run by the Fundación Museos de la Ciudad, a nonprofit acting on commission of the Quito municipality. Admission is free.
watch: Housed in the old military hospital, San Juan district. Part of the Sistema de Museos Quito. No controversy found.
records_note: The foundation running it posts yearly accountability reports from 2016 to 2025 with budgets and transparency files; it names no funders and no board.

name: Centro de Arte Fundación Ortiz-Gurdián
funding: Private family foundation (founded 1996, León museum opened 2000) paid for by founders Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga and Patricia Gurdián, Banpro and Grupo Promerica.
watch: Banking money (Banpro/Promerica, not under campaign). Ortega regime arrested Banpro's general manager in June 2021.
records_note: No reports or accounts found; no funder list beyond Banpro's credit on the Managua centre; the family board is named on the home page.

name: Centro Pecci
funding: Funded by the City of Prato and the Tuscany region.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2016 to 2024 and accounts 2016 to 2026, lists a seven-member board, and names its partners and sponsors, including PwC, undated.

name: Chale Wote Street Art Festival
funding: Free street festival (15th edition Aug 2025) by ACCRA [dot] ALT; 2023 supported by Ghana's tourism ministry, Ghana Tourism Authority, Citi FM, Institut Français.
watch: Accra's street art festival, held in Jamestown since 2011. The Ghana Tourism Authority helped keep the 2023 edition going.
records_note: The organiser's site posts no reports, accounts or board, and names supporters only inside festival announcements, not on a standing funder page.
